- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- When true outcome shows sharp spikes (e.g., >15% from prior), model often overestimates continuation — cap forecast rise to 5–10% above prior peak.  
- If history shows mean-reverting pattern (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), forecast should not drift >10% above mean unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong volatility or sentiment shift, reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±5% deviation from recent 5-day average.  
- If sentiment history is flat (0.00) and forecast is trending, check for lag: if true outcome diverges >10% from forecast after 5–7 days, adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day mean.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast peaks >10% above prior high, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- For sentiment = 0.00, forecast should be anchored to recent 7-day average unless market shows clear momentum.
